items.abstract_or_text: common: honor HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY env vars in http client (#21752) * common: honor HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY env vars in http client common_http_client() was ignoring standard proxy env vars, causing downloads via -hf and similar flags to fail silently in environments behind an HTTP proxy (corporate networks, air-gapped infra, etc.). Checks HTTPS_PROXY/https_proxy for https:// URLs and HTTP_PROXY/http_proxy for http:// URLs, in that order. If a proxy URL is set and parseable, passes it to httplib's set_proxy() and set_proxy_basic_auth() as appropriate. Malformed proxy URLs are silently ignored so existing callers aren't affected. Fixes #21694 * common: drop misleading comment about generic proxy fallback The comment referenced a 'generic one' that doesn't exist in the code — both HTTP_PROXY and HTTPS_PROXY are scheme-specific. Reviewer noted the mismatch. Addresses review feedback from @ServeurpersoCom. * common : warn when the proxy URL from the environment is malformed * common : honor NO_PROXY when selecting the http proxy * ci : retrigger checks (test-thread-safety flake) * common : bypass the proxy for loopback destinations llama cli talks to its spawned server on 127.0.0.1 through common_http_client, so with HTTP_PROXY set and no NO_PROXY the health polling went to the corporate proxy, which rejects loopback targets, and the wait loop never exits ("Loading model..." hangs forever). A remote proxy can never reach the client machine's own loopback, so these destinations are now always contacted directly, before NO_PROXY is consulted: localhost, *.localhost, 127.0.0.0/8, ::1 and 0.0.0.0. Similar to Go's net/http. Proxy handling for downloads and remote --server-base endpoints is unchanged. Signed-off-by: texasich * docs: move proxy tip from README to server docs per review: the top level README stays lean; the proxy howto now lives with the server docs under Usage Signed-off-by: texasich --------- Signed-off-by: texasich Co-authored-by: texasich Co-authored-by: texasich Co-authored-by: marecabo **Website:** - items.abstract_or_text: model: add Muse Spark Open (text, vision and audio) (#30616) * model: add Muse Spark Open (text, vision and audio) Muse Spark Open is a latent space MoE: the residual stream stays at 8192 while the 256 experts live in 4096, with a projection down and up around them, top-8 sigmoid routing with a correction bias. Attention interleaves three sliding layers at a 2048 window with rope for one global layer without rope, with a sigmoid output gate and a weightless QK-norm. Residuals are norm preserving, their gate is folded at conversion time. Vision reuses the Muse Glimmer tower. Audio is a causal convolutional pyramid with no attention and no spectrogram, four stages folding 16, 6, 5 and 4 samples into the channel dim, one embedding per 80 ms of 24 kHz. The quantizer keeps the latent projections and the attention gate at Q8_0, a little over 1% of the weights, since the whole residual stream passes through them and the low-bit types turned the output into a repeating loop. The model saver writes the post norm epsilon, and the arch is registered in test-llama-archs. items.abstract_or_text: server: save only restorable slot states to the prompt cache (#30498) * server: save only restorable slot states to the prompt cache The idle-slot save loop stores every idle slot whenever a task starts, while only completion tasks restore from the prompt cache. Rerank, embedding, decision and infill states fill the cache up to its limit without ever being read back, and slots already cached are offered again at every task start. Each slot now tracks with cache_pending whether its state is restorable and missing from the cache: a completion release or an explicit slot restore sets it, prompt_save consumes it, prompt_clear resets it. Both save paths share this rule, and the LRU path restores only for completion tasks. * server: test that decision slots skip the prompt cache Decision tasks never mark their slot as cacheable, so starting new tasks must not save their idle slots to the RAM prompt cache, with or without a unified KV cache. * server: restore any reusing task from the prompt cache Embedding and rerank tasks never reuse their state, so their slots are cleared on release like child slots and the cache only holds states that a later task can restore. Infill and decision tasks now restore from the cache too, which replaces the cache_pending flag. Decision models disable the prompt cache unless --cache-ram is given, since their states seldom repeat. **Website:** - **Attestations:** - **macOS/iOS:** - [macOS Apple Silicon (arm64)](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/download/b11642/llama-b11642-bin-macos-arm64.tar.gz) - items.abstract_or_text: sycl: IQ3 code reorder (#29107) * sycl: persistent IQ3_S/IQ3_XXS weight reorder for SYCL decode and prefill Add persistent reordered weight layouts for IQ3_S and IQ3_XXS. Weights are reordered once at load time; the reordered MMVQ dot products then walk dense super-blocks with dp4a and SWAR sign expansion instead of gathering bits from the interleaved standard layout. Reorder-aware dequantization feeds the batched prefill GEMMs so prompt processing sees the same benefit. Also harden the oneDNN build check: a missing DNNL package or a CPU-only DNNL build now fails at configure time instead of silently producing a degraded backend. Measured on Intel Arc Pro B70 with Qwen3.8-27B-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_S (MTP), -ngl 999 -b 4096 -ub 1024 -fa on: tg256 @ 0 ctx 12.92 -> 23.54 tok/s (+82%) tg256 @ 9,216 12.33 -> 21.69 tok/s (+76%) tg256 @ 64,000 9.76 -> 14.91 tok/s (+53%) pp8192 833.9 -> 833.6 tok/s (flat) Qwen3.5-9B Q4_K_M / Q3_K_M are unchanged within noise (largest delta -0.5% pp, tg flat), so standard quants are not affected. The MMVQ GLU fusion widening and rms_norm+scale fusion are intentionally not part of this change; master already carries them via #28931. * removing wait as per review request * sycl : fix fusion.cpp line ending **Website:** -
